In machine learning the equivalent of eating endless lemon tarts is overfitting a model.  It’s easy and tempting and if you’re not careful it will come back to haunt you.

Overfitting is when you put in so much effort that you capture all the idiosyncracies of your sample data.  Those things that are  idiosyncratic are not really there in the underlying population (or may be there but overpowered by other effects) but in your sample they are very important, so you end up modelling them.

The problem is that what is idiosyncratic in the sample probably won’t be there in the next data set you get.  So all the attention and effort you put into modelling it is mostly wasted, and what’s worse you end up with a model that performs badly on new unseen data.

The equivalent of having a quarterly “treat day” at the lemon tart bakery is to hold back some of your data to validate your model.  You use some to build it, but then test how it performs on data it has never seen before.

As well as this you can do various things in how you build your models that will help – penalising complexity, early stopping, using nonparametric methods* like decision trees, using Bayesian priors, using cross-validation and more.

There are a ton of heuristics but I think the best general principle is not to be impressed with how good your model looks on the data you used to build it.  You need to be impressed by how good it is on data that has never seen during model creation.

That way you’ll be having “treats” rather than gorging yourself all the time, and you’ll be healthy in the long run.

> I love how the sharp filling perfectly complements the buttery crust—the combination of flavors and textures is just right to me.

這句實際上是可行的，但更常見或更地道的說法是：

## **Dairy-Free Crust**

Traditional pastry uses butter, but there are several ways to make a rich, flaky crust without it:

### **1. Use a Shortening or Plant-Based Margarine**
• **Vegetable shortening** (dairy-free and often easier to work with than oils).
• **Coconut oil** (solid at room temperature; gives a slightly coconutty flavor, best in moderation).
• **Vegan butter or margarine** (such as Earth Balance or Miyoko’s).

**Tip:** For flakiness, you can use a mix of solid fat (like coconut oil or vegan butter) and a little olive or canola oil in your dough.

**Basic Dairy-Free Crust Recipe:**
1. Combine 1 ¼ cups flour, ¼ tsp salt.
2. Cut in ½ cup solid fat (vegan butter or shortening) until crumbly.
3. Add 3-4 Tbsp cold oil (like canola or olive) and mix until dough comes together.
4. Add ¼-⅓ cup ice water, one tablespoon at a time, until dough holds together.
5. Chill, roll out, and line tart pan as usual.

---

Traditional lemon curd uses eggs and butter. But you can substitute the butter effectively:

### **1. Coconut Oil or Vegan Butter**
Replace the melted butter in your lemon curd recipe with an equal amount of **melted coconut oil or vegan butter**.

### **2. Egg-Based Filling (Vegan Optional)**
Classic lemon curd is custard-like, made with eggs and sugar cooked with lemon juice in the presence of butter.
- For a **dairy-free (but not vegan)** version, simply replace butter with coconut oil or vegan butter.

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    it = iter(data)
    n = int(next(it))
    x = int(next(it))

    best_idx = -1        # index of the best candidate found so far
    best_b = -1          # highest beauty among the candidates
    best_s = -1          # among those with best_b, highest sweetness

    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        b = int(next(it))
        s = int(next(it))
        if b >= x and s >= x:                # only Really nice tarts are considered
            if b > best_b:                   # higher beauty is better
                best_b = b
                best_s = s
                best_idx = i
            elif b == best_b and s > best_s: # same beauty, higher sweetness
                best_s = s
                best_idx = i
            # if both beauty and sweetness are equal, keep the smaller index (already enforced by scanning order)

    print(best_idx)

if __name__ == "__main__":

SET UP

Class Lemon:

Methods

Add a method to take a bite of the lemon tart.
Add a method to see if it is time to take another bite.
Tests

Write a program that creates an instance of LemonTart with a shortcrust and a little amount of filling.
Then repeatedly take a bite of the lemon tart and display its state until it is all gone.
Requirements

The crust can be shortcrust, puff, or crumble.
The amount of filling can be a little, medium, or a lot.
There are three stages of the lemon tart:
A tart with a fully intact crust, lots of filling, and a juice center.
A tart with lots of filling and a broken crust.
A tart with no filling and a broken crust.
Taking a bite of a tart in the first stage decreases the amount of filling by one degree (that is, from a lot to medium or from medium to a little) and leaves the crust intact.
Taking a bite of a tart in the second stage breaks the crust and decreases the amount of filling by one degree.
Taking a bite of a tart in the third stage does nothing.
Every two bites, the tart is checked and advanced to the next stage if necessary.
Each time a bite is taken the action should be printed.
Each time the stage changes, the new stage should be printed.
Sample Run

This is not a custardy French-style tart, nor the crunchy sugar-crusted version that’;s popular in England. Lemon Tart

for the crust
6 oz. butter
6 oz. powdered sugar
2 eggs
8 oz. (about 2 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour

for the filling
12 unwaxed lemons
1 1/4 pounds sugar
4 large egg yolks
1/2 cup water
Pinch of salt

Instructions

Divide in two disks, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 350 degrees. Have ready a 10-inch tart pan with a removable bottom. On a work surface, roll out one of the disks of dough and line the tart pan with it, taking care that the dough hangs over the edges a bit. Prick the bottom all over with the tines of a fork.
